sentences.text:
The petitioner is the accused in C.C.No.756/2021 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate -I,
Kottayam (Trial Court) which originates from Crime No.220/2020 registered by the Kumarakom Police Station, Kottayam, alleging the commission of the the offence punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text:
Judicial First Class Magistrate -I,
Kottayam (Trial Court)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The petitioner states that, the petitioner had not received any summons from the Trial Court because he is employed in Gujarat.

The petitioner has now learnt that a non-bailable warrant has been issued against him and steps under Section 82, 83 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C),
are also initiated.
The petitioner proposes to surrender before the Trial Court and get himself enlarged on bail.
However, the petitioner is apprehensive that his applications may not be considered on the date of surrender, CRL.MC NO. 11114 OF 2025 3 2025:KER:94537 and he may be remanded to judicial custody.

Hence, the Crl.M.C.
3. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

4. On a consideration of the facts and the materials on record, without expressing anything on the merits of the matter, I dispose of the Crl.M.C, by permitting the petitioner to surrender before the Trial Court within two weeks from today (06.12.2025) and file applications to recall the non- bailable warrant, the Sections 82, 83 Cr.P.C. steps, and to enlarge him on bail.

If such applications are filed, after serving advance copies on the learned Public Prosecutor, the Trial Court is directed to consider and dispose of the applications, in accordance with law, and as expeditiously as possible,
on the same day the petitioner surrenders before the Trial Court.

Sd/-
C.S.DIAS,JUDGE SCB/06.12.25.
